C0.quote: strategyproof facility location in two dimensions
C0.note: Strategyproof mechanisms for facility location, framed as voting/approximate mechanism design (median mechanisms, voting scheme characterisations). Borderline vs. facility location, but treated as eligible: strategic aspects of aggregating agents' reported ideal points.

C1.quote: has the lowest worst-case approximation ratio in the class of deterministic
C1.note: Main results are approximation ratios (WD) of strategyproof mechanisms; Theorem 1 optimality within strategyproof class uses characterisations (AX) and strategyproofness. AL is a weak fit (approximation of optimum, not computing) so AL is included only loosely.

C2.1.value: ideal points; reports of ideal points (profile of ideal points)
C2.1.quote: Let x be the profile of ideal points

C2.2.quote: each agent has an ideal point xi ∈ X for a facility
C2.2.note: Input is a point in R^2 (ideal point report); none of the listed formats.

C2.3.quote: Each agent’s preference is defined by its ideal point

C2.4.quote: no agent can benefit by misreporting her ideal point
C2.4.note: Mechanism is a function of X^n applied to ideal points directly; strategyproofness definition mentions misreporting but no separate notation for reports vs ideal points; the input equals the ideal point in notation. Doubt between DIST and IDU; chose IDU because notation is not separate.

C3.1.quote: no agent can benefit by misreporting her ideal point
C3.1.note: Strategyproofness is a property considered (incentive analysis), while approximation ratio analyses evaluate the mechanism on the profile of ideal points without strategic behaviour modelled. Doubt: ALL vs SOME; SOME chosen because the AR computations take profiles as given.

C3.2.note: Non-strategic analyses (approximation ratios) are justified implicitly by strategyproofness but no explicit statement that agents submit their ideal point.

C4.1.note: Input format is OTH, not ordinal/approval.

C5.1.note: Approximation ratio of social cost (utilitarian, p-norm) is the evaluation criterion; social cost is the welfare-type criterion.

C5.2.quote: The social cost of locating the facility at y under profile
C5.2.note: Social cost computed on the profile of ideal points, which is also what the mechanism takes as input; no statement relating reports to ideal points beyond strategyproofness.

VOT.quote_behav: Since agents may lie about their ideal points if it benefits them
VOT.note: Strategyproofness is dominant-strategy, implying any information; information not specified.

DES.quote_behav: A central planner wishes to locate the facility to minimize the social cost
DES.note: Planner chooses a mechanism, constrained to strategyproof ones, to minimise worst-case approximation ratio; modelled explicitly as objective.

C7.1.note: Voters are strategic (in the strategyproofness sense) and the planner optimises; neither is NONSTRAT.

C8.1.quote: no agent can benefit by misreporting her ideal point, regardless of the reports

C8.2.quote: A mechanism f is strategyproof if for all i ∈ N

C9.1.note: Claims of optimality of a rule, a mild recommendation of which rule to use.

C9.2.note: Optimality for social cost on true ideal points under strategyproofness needs the assumption that truthful reporting is what agents do (relation of inputs to ideal points) and that cost equals Euclidean distance; the former is only implicit via strategyproofness, not stated as an assumption.
